brief: Today's posts centered on Claude's new product updates, including Claude Data, Whiteboards, Sheets and interactive connectors, alongside Gemini 4 Carbon's launch and early reviews. Vercel's security review and Peter Steinberger's post on 35,000 newly found vulnerabilities also drew attention to AI-driven security scanning.

themes.label: Claude product updates
themes.summary: Builders pointed to Claude Data becoming generally available, plus interactive connectors that open tools like Adobe, Atlassian and Box inside Claude.

themes.label: Gemini 4 Carbon
themes.summary: Dan Shipper's team tested Gemini 4 Carbon, finding it a stronger coder than Argon but not always knowing when to stop, while Josh Woodward noted its rollout to Ultra subscribers.

themes.label: AI-driven security scanning
themes.summary: Builders described AI agents finding and fixing large numbers of vulnerabilities, from Vercel's security review to a company's re-run with GPT-6 Astra.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Argued that agent swarms will separate teams that adopt them from those that don't. He also announced a Box and Anthropic partnership for read/write access to Box files through Claude via MCP.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Reported that Vercel Security Review found 57,897 vulnerabilities in under a week, with an agent patching 14,665 of them. He also said new programming languages will emerge with agents.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary: Announced Claude Data is generally available on paid plans, and rolled out interactive connectors and Whiteboards, Sheets and Data updates.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Published a day-zero vibe check of Gemini 4 Carbon from testing at Every, including a coding benchmark and a nearly 4.5-hour run that overreached its task list.

builders.name: Latent Space
builders.summary: Published a podcast with Zeno Rocha of Resend on designing for agents, covering Resend's growth to 4.3 million users.

builders.name: Peter Steinberger
builders.summary: Shared a report that a company's re-run of diagnostics with GPT-6 Astra confirmed 35,000 new vulnerabilities after earlier fixes.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Asked Zeno Rocha why agents keep choosing Resend, and teased a keynote at the AIE live stream on Thursday.

builders.name: Ryo Lu
builders.summary: Posted that people working together is where the magic happens rather than siloed agents, and shared a few personal reflections.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Said the field needs fewer one-shot demos and more tools for collaborating with models.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Announced that Gemini 4 Carbon is available to Ultra subscribers worldwide in the Gemini app.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Recommended a Railway post-mortem as a must read for infra providers, and posted some personal and minor items.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Posted brief, engagement-style messages about small businesses and labs innovating together, with no substantive content.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Praised Anthropic's focus on accelerating disease cures and defended tasteful use of AI in game development.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Posted a single short reply that the most successful friends tend to have the most intense hobbies.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Shared two short product tips: share work in progress early, and most users who don't return have forgotten the product exists.

builders.name: Nan Yu
builders.summary: Highlighted a dictation app's support for the Apple dictation key and several shortcut modes.
